body:
A Dictionary can contain both `int` and `String` keys at the same time (e.g. `0` and `"0"`). If `get_indexed` would try to match against stringified keys then it would be ambiguous (+such matching would need to be done somehow, thus it would add an overhead, whether it would be iterating over all keys and checking against stringified key (in case of no match), or whether it would cache hashes for stringified keys, or whatever else; aka not performance friendly, but that's beside the point here).

```gdscript
@tool
extends EditorScript

var d := {
	0: "int",
	0.0: "float",
	"0": "String",
	#&"0": "StringName", # If uncommented: Error at (8, 5): Key "0" was already used in this dictionary (at line 7).
	^"0": "NodePath",
}

func _run() -> void:
	print(get_indexed("d:0")) # String
```

I think the current behavior needs to be documented (makes sense to clarify for both Dictionary and Array).
Not sure whether in docs for `get_indexed`/`set_indexed` or `NodePath` (or maybe Dictionary/Array).
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/778cf54dabd8a9e25b698a87036ab8604183f303/doc/classes/Object.xml#L606-L628
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/778cf54dabd8a9e25b698a87036ab8604183f303/doc/classes/Object.xml#L927-L948
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/778cf54dabd8a9e25b698a87036ab8604183f303/doc/classes/NodePath.xml#L6-L36

What I find inconsistent is that it works for Dictionaries that have a String key. 
This makes String the assumed default key-type for Dictionaries.
It even works on non-typed Dictionaries with mixed key-types where it returns the key string(0) but not int(0). (see output below and expanded example project)

This is not true for Arrays that always have int as the default key type. 
So I would expect them to operate the same way as Dictionaries. 
ArrayPath:IntIndex e.g MyArray:0 should return a value when MyDict:Key0 returns a value.

If the get_indexed and set_indexed functions can never return a value for dictionary elements that have a different key type than String it should be mentioned somewhere. It should also be mentioned that Array will never return a value when addressing with an index like MyArray:IntIndex.

[issue-node-path v2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25718593/issue-node-path.v2.zip)
